items.title: The Help Page Students Could Not Search

A.question: What is the main lesson of the passage?
A.answer: A help page became easier to use when its headings matched the everyday words students actually searched for.
A.evidence: The page needed not more information but words that matched the questions users actually asked.
A.evidenceJp: 必要だったのは情報を増やすことではなく、利用者が実際に尋ねる言葉に合わせることでした。
A.reason: The conclusion identifies matching user language, not adding content, as the key improvement.

A.question: Why did the computer team watch three students search the help page?
A.answer: To learn why repeated questions continued even though the answers were already on the page.
A.evidence: The computer team first thought students were not reading the page. Three students tried to find answers while team members watched.
A.evidenceJp: コンピュータ担当は最初、生徒がページを読んでいないのだと考えました。三人の生徒に答えを探してもらい、その様子を観察しました。
A.reason: Observation tested the assumption that students were simply ignoring the page.

A.question: Which statement is true according to the passage?
A.answer: The team kept the detailed explanations but changed formal headings into everyday phrases.
A.evidence: The team kept the detailed explanations and changed the headings to everyday phrases such as “I forgot my password” and “When is the library open?”
A.evidenceJp: 詳しい説明は残し、見出しを「パスワードを忘れた」「図書館は何時まで開いている？」のような日常的な表現へ変えました。
A.reason: The solution changed search language while preserving the underlying information.

A.question: Why did formal office terms make the page difficult to search?
A.answer: Students searched with ordinary question phrases, so their words did not match the formal headings.
A.evidence: The information was there, but every heading used formal office terms that students did not type into the search box.
A.evidenceJp: 情報はありましたが、見出しがすべて事務的な表現で、生徒が検索欄に入れる言葉とは違っていました。
A.reason: Search depends on overlap between what users type and the words used to label the information.

A.question: How many students tested the search while team members watched?
A.evidence: Three students tried to find answers while team members watched.
A.evidenceJp: 三人の生徒に答えを探してもらい、その様子を観察しました。

B.question: In “The information was there,” what information is meant?
B.answer: The answers to common questions such as password changes, club forms, and library hours.
B.evidence: A school website had a help page with answers to many common questions. Students still sent repeated messages about password changes, club forms, and library hours.
B.evidenceJp: 学校のウェブサイトには、よくある質問への答えをまとめた案内ページがありました。それでも生徒から、パスワード変更、部活動の書類、図書館の時間について同じ質問が何度も届きました。
B.reason: The phrase refers to the existing answers that students were failing to find.

B.question: Complete the summary: The help page already contained enough information, but its headings used ____ instead of the language students searched with.
B.evidence: The information was there, but every heading used formal office terms that students did not type into the search box.
B.evidenceJp: 情報はありましたが、見出しがすべて事務的な表現で、生徒が検索欄に入れる言葉とは違っていました。
B.reason: The mismatch in wording was the central search problem.

B.question: Complete the example heading: “I forgot my ____.”
B.evidence: The team kept the detailed explanations and changed the headings to everyday phrases such as “I forgot my password” and “When is the library open?”
B.evidenceJp: 詳しい説明は残し、見出しを「パスワードを忘れた」「図書館は何時まで開いている？」のような日常的な表現へ変えました。
B.reason: The everyday heading is quoted directly.

B.question: Where would this sentence fit best: “The users and the page were using different words for the same needs.”
B.answer: After the sentence explaining that students did not type the formal office terms into the search box.
B.evidence: The information was there, but every heading used formal office terms that students did not type into the search box. The team kept the detailed explanations and changed the headings to everyday phrases such as “I forgot my password” and “When is the library open?”
B.evidenceJp: 情報はありましたが、見出しがすべて事務的な表現で、生徒が検索欄に入れる言葉とは違っていました。詳しい説明は残し、見出しを「パスワードを忘れた」「図書館は何時まで開いている？」のような日常的な表現へ変えました。
B.reason: The sentence summarizes the mismatch immediately before the team fixes it.

B.question: What should the team do when adding a new help topic?
B.answer: Use a heading that reflects how students naturally phrase the question, while keeping detailed information underneath.
B.evidence: The team kept the detailed explanations and changed the headings to everyday phrases such as “I forgot my password” and “When is the library open?”
B.evidenceJp: 詳しい説明は残し、見出しを「パスワードを忘れた」「図書館は何時まで開いている？」のような日常的な表現へ変えました。
B.reason: The successful redesign combines searchable everyday language with detailed answers.
